pr_title: samples: echo_server: Enable USB by the application
pr_body:
This commit allows let build echo_server sample with overlay-netusb.conf.
USB subsystem must be enabled by the application.

Fixes #39195

issue_context.title: USB: netusb: example echo_server not working as expected
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

Since commit 57084f32a13bebda80fd7934ae245945910828af the echo_server example will not working anymore with the netusb overlay configuration. We still missing the same change as seen on the zperf example that enable USB by the application.

A clear and concise description of what the bug is.
What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue?


**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. ```
   west build -d build/zm-f767zi-socket-echo-server-sample \
              --cmake-only -b nucleo_f767zi \
                 ./zephyr/samples/net/sockets/echo_server \
                 -- -DCONF_FILE="prj.conf overlay-netusb.conf" \
                    -DCONFIG_ETH_STM32_HAL=n
   ```
2. `west build -d build/zm-f767zi-socket-echo-server-sample -t all`
3. `west flash -d build/zm-f767zi-socket-echo-server-sample`
4. See error (logs below, manual interface up)


**Expected behavior**

Network interface 1 is up and running after power on or reset, `net iface show 1` should not print `Interface is down.`, and also on USB host side the new USB Ethernet device can be detected and used.


**Impact**

Annoying, because the example does not work without further ado.

**Infected releases: all since v2.4**


**Logs and console output**

*Power on log and interface status:*
> ```
> *** Booting Zephyr OS build v2.7.0-rc3-304-gd198da7bb4ba  ***
> [00:00:00.000,000] <inf> usb_net: netusb initialized
> [00:00:00.006,000] <inf> net_echo_server_sample: Run echo server
> [00:00:00.006,000] <inf> net_echo_server_sample: Waiting network to be connected
> ```
`uart:~$ net iface show 1`
> ```
> Interface 0x20021eb8 (Ethernet) [1]
> ===================================
> Interface is down.
> Link addr : 00:00:5E:00:53:00
> MTU       : 1500
> Flags     : NO_AUTO_START,IPv4,IPv6
> Ethernet capabilities supported:
> IPv6 unicast addresses (max 3):
>         <none>
> IPv6 multicast addresses (max 4):
>         <none>
> IPv6 prefixes (max 2):
>         <none>
> IPv4 unicast addresses (max 1):
>         <none>
> IPv4 multicast addresses (max 1):
>         <none>
> ```

*Manual interface up:*
`uart:~$ net iface up 1`
> ```
> Interface 1 is up
> [00:11:38.116,000] <err> usb_net: interface disabled
> [00:11:38.116,000] <err> usb_net: interface disabled
> [00:11:38.117,000] <err> usb_net: interface disabled
> [00:11:38.117,000] <err> usb_net: interface disabled
> [00:11:38.217,000] <inf> net_echo_server_sample: Network connected
> [00:11:38.217,000] <inf> net_echo_server_sample: Starting...
> [00:11:38.217,000] <inf> net_echo_server_sample: Waiting for TCP connection on port 4242 (IPv6)...
> [00:11:38.217,000] <inf> net_echo_server_sample: Waiting for TCP connection on port 4242 (IPv4)...
> [00:11:38.217,000] <inf> net_echo_server_sample: Waiting for UDP packets on port 4242 (IPv6)...
> [00:11:38.218,000] <inf> net_echo_server_sample: Waiting for UDP packets on port 4242 (IPv4)...
> [00:11:39.117,000] <err> usb_net: interface disabled
> [00:11:40.117,000] <err> usb_net: interface disabled
> ```

Now on USB host side (Linux system) the USB device can't or better will not enumerated. That makes sense as long as the Zephyr USB stack is not running because of missing trigger by application.

`user@host:folder$ lsusb -d 2fe3:0100 || echo "NOT FOUND"`
> ```
> NOT FOUND
> ```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: MacOS
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK 0.13.1
 - Commit SHA used: d198da7bb4bafdd185df5122150a843c1dcea5b1

**Additional context**
Also see #27427.

review_comments: For anyone wondering (like me) why is this needed for USB, `config NET_CONFIG_AUTO_INIT` has `default n if USB_DEVICE_NETWORK`
